newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West spot power rises with unit outages.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West spot power rises with unit outages.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the Midwestern U.S. climbed again Wednesday on continued cold weather, generation unit outages and reports of contraints on power exports from Canada, sources said.

In Illinois, Commonwealth Edison reduced power at its 789 megawatt Quad Cities nuclear unit 2, and Central Illinois Public Service idled its 900 megawatt Coffeen coal-fired plant for two to three days for boiler tube leak repairs.
Also, Manitoba Hydro was said to be having problems exporting power out of Canada into the U.S., although the company would not confirm the reports.

Peak, non-firm power for Thursday delivery in the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) region were said to have traded near $20.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) Wednesday morning, but then surged higher with reports of $26.00 bids for 16-hour Thursday blocks going unanswered.
MAPP next-day power had been talked at $17.00-19.50 per MWh on Tuesday.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power was also assessed higher at $11.00-12.00 from $9.50-11.50 on Tuesday, the brokers and marketers said.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), non-firm peak power for Thursday delivery was said to be higher at $19.00-21.00 from $17.00-19.50 on Tuesday, the sources said.
Off-peak next day MAIN power was pegged higher at $12.00-14.00 from $11.50-13.00 on Tuesday.

In the East Central Area Coordination Agreement (ECAR), peak, non-firm electricity prices for Thursday delivery were said to be stronger at $18.00-22.00 per MWh from $17.00-19.00 on Tuesday, the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was talked steady in the $12.50-14.00 area, the sources said.
November ECAR prices held at $17.25-17.55, while December was pegged steady near $18.70-19.10.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), peak, non-firm power for Thursday delivery was assessed stronger at $23.00-26.00 from talk at $21.00-25.00 on Tuesday, the sources said.
Off-peak prices in SPP held steady in the $12.00-14.00 area, the sources said.
"With the cold weather and seasonal outages, everybody seems to have just enough generation to cover their own needs," one Mid-West electricity broker said.
December SPP was also discussed higher at $21.00-21.30 from $20.50-20.75 on Tuesday, the sources said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
